item.title: Why a Pure-Rust HTML-to-PDF Engine Could Be a Bigger Deal Than Most Developers Realize
item.description: Still using headless Chromium for PDF generation? That might change soon. A lightweight Rust library is redefining document rendering boundaries—it runs on the edge, compiles to WASM, and needs no browser.

item.title: Java's Quiet Revolution: How February 2026 Changed Everything You Thought You Knew About the JVM
item.description: February 2026 brings a quiet revolution to the Java ecosystem: JEP 531 lazy constants optimize startup performance, TornadoVM 3.0 brings Java to GPUs, and Chicory enables WebAssembly-JVM interoperability. From Open Liberty security patches to Quarkus integrating Project Leyden, Java is redefining itself for the cloud-native and AI era.

item.title: WebGPU Performance Test: 23x Faster than WebAssembly - The Browser Computing Revolution
item.description: Real-world test shows WebGPU is 23x faster than WebAssembly. This article explains GPU parallel computing principles and implementation details through three actual case studies of data visualization, image processing, and physics simulation.

item.title: Will WASM + Rust Replace Linux Containers? Performance, Security, Cold Starts, and Trade‑offs
item.description: Plain‑English notes and references for WASM + Rust vs Linux containers: performance, security, cold starts, ecosystem, and standards.

item.title: Rust 1.91.1: Critical Wasm and illumos Fixes and Why You Should Upgrade
item.description: A plain‑English explanation of the two regressions fixed in Rust 1.91.1 around WebAssembly imports and Cargo target directory locking on illumos, what risks they introduced, and why even beginners should move off 1.91.0.
